mainTopic: Squeezing on שבת: which juices count as a liquid, whether one person's habit or intent matters, and whether a liquid that goes into food counts as food
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא. It allows squeezing plums, quinces, and crab apples on שבת, but not pomegranates, because the household of מנשיא בר מנחם squeezed pomegranates. The גמרא shows that this ברייתא fits the חכמים, since fruits not normally squeezed may be squeezed even לכתחילה. רב נחמן rules like the household of מנשיא בר מנחם. רבא objects that one family is not most of the world. A proof from thorns grown in ערביא is rejected, because a whole country differs from one family. The גמרא then suggests that once a person treats a juice as important it counts as a liquid, based on רב חסדא's ruling about beet juice in a מקוה. רב פפא explains that ruling differently, and a parallel argument follows about whether מוחל (olive discharge) is a liquid. Next, שמואל allows squeezing grapes into a pot of food but not into an empty bowl, and רב חסדא applies this to milking a goat: a liquid that goes into food counts as food. רמי בר חמא challenges this rule from a זב who milks a goat, and the challenge is answered. רבינא then begins a new challenge that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: some fruits may be squeezed, but not pomegranates
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by permitting squeezing of plums, quinces, and crab apples, but not pomegranates, because one well-known household squeezed pomegranates for juice.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may squeeze plums, quinces, and crab apples, but not pomegranates. The household of מנשיא בר מנחם used to squeeze pomegranates.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it brought as proof. The ברייתא shows that fruits people do not normally squeeze may be squeezed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on whether people normally squeeze a fruit for its juice. Plums, quinces, and crab apples are not normally squeezed, so squeezing them is not a real act of 'extracting juice.' Pomegranates are different, because there were people (the household of מנשיא בר מנחם) who squeezed them for juice.

keyTerms.meaning: a type of fruit (plums, as some explain)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The beginning of the ברייתא ('one may squeeze...') is on the previous page.

phrases.english: [One may squeeze] plums, quinces, and crab apples,
but not pomegranates,
for those of the house of Menashya bar Menachem
would squeeze pomegranates.
phrases.notes: This shows that pomegranates are sometimes squeezed for juice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא cited on the previous page as support for the view that the חכמים permit squeezing fruits not normally squeezed.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים allow squeezing fruits that are not normally squeezed for juice
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing plums, quinces, and crab apples as permitted, and excluding pomegranates

steps.title: Maybe this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the ברייתא follows the חכמים. Perhaps it reflects רבי יהודה's more lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this ברייתא follows the חכמים? Maybe it follows רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof. A lenient ברייתא might belong to רבי יהודה, who is known to be lenient about fruit juices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the ברייתא reflects the view of the חכמים. רבי יהודה is lenient about juice from fruits meant for eating. So the lenient ruling could just be his opinion, which would prove nothing about the חכמים.

phrases.english: And from where [do we know] that it is [the view of] the Rabbis?
Perhaps it is [the view of] Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּרַבָּנַן הִיא, דִּילְמָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof brought in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא reflects the חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The lenient ruling might come from רבי יהודה, whose view is already known to be lenient. If so, it proves nothing about the חכמים.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה only permitted juice that came out on its own
steps.stepSummary: Even if the ברייתא were רבי יהודה's, he only permitted juice that seeped out by itself. Permitting active squeezing must rest on a different reason: these fruits are not normally squeezed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it be רבי יהודה. You only heard him permit juice that came out by itself. Did you ever hear him permit squeezing from the start? Rather, you must say the reason is that these fruits are not normally squeezed, so it is permitted even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה alone cannot explain the ברייתא. The ברייתא permits active squeezing, which רבי יהודה never permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's leniency was only about juice that leaked out on its own. The ברייתא goes further and permits squeezing לכתחילה. So the ברייתא's real reason must be that these fruits are not normally squeezed, and that reason has nothing to do with רבי יהודה's special leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: [the juices] came out on their own

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'juice that came out by itself' with 'squeezing on purpose.' רבי יהודה was only lenient about the first. The ברייתא permits the second.

phrases.english: And let it also be Rabbi Yehuda;
say that you heard Rabbi Yehuda [permit]
[juices that] came out on their own;
did you hear him [permit] squeezing from the start?!
Rather, what must you say?
Since they are not [fruits] meant for squeezing,
[it is permitted] even from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by showing that רבי יהודה's view cannot explain the ברייתא by itself.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the true reason behind the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's leniency comes from רבי יהודה's known leniency.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency comes from the fact that these fruits are not normally squeezed. That reason does not depend on רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The same reason works for the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The reason 'not normally squeezed' fits the חכמים just as well, so the ברייתא can be theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say it follows the חכמים: since these fruits are not normally squeezed, it is permitted even from the start. Learn from this that it is the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. The reason it just found works equally well for the חכמים, so the ברייתא is a valid proof about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason behind the ruling is the type of fruit, not רבי יהודה's special leniency. So nothing ties the ברייתא to רבי יהודה. The חכמים also agree that fruits not normally squeezed may be squeezed.

phrases.english: Even if you say [it is] the Rabbis,
since they are not [fruits] meant for squeezing,
[it is permitted] even from the start.
Learn from it that it is [the view of] the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reason found in step 3 to the חכמים, completing the answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the shared reason to the חכמים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might only show רבי יהודה's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא fits the חכמים, so it proves the חכמים permit squeezing fruits not normally squeezed.

steps.title: Conclusion: the ברייתא follows the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the conclusion: the ברייתא reflects the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this back-and-forth by agreeing that the proof stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The short 'שמע מינה' at the end confirms the inference without any further challenge. The חכמים agree that fruits not normally squeezed may be squeezed on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Fruits that people do not normally squeeze (plums, quinces, crab apples) may be squeezed on שבת, even according to the חכמים. Pomegranates are excluded because some people do squeeze them.

phrases.english: Learn from it [indeed].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the inference reached in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא follows the חכמים. They permit squeezing fruits not normally squeezed, but not pomegranates.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules like the household of מנשיא בר מנחם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the line about the household of מנשיא בר מנחם. רב נחמן then rules that the הלכה follows it, so pomegranates count as fruit that is squeezed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The household of מנשיא בר מנחם used to squeeze pomegranates. רב נחמן said: the הלכה follows the household of מנשיא בר מנחם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to one detail of the ברייתא, the pomegranate-squeezing household, to discuss it on its own. רב נחמן rules that their practice decides the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן means that because this household squeezed pomegranates, pomegranates count as a squeezed fruit. So squeezing them on שבת is forbidden. This raises a new question: can one family's habit set the הלכה?

keyTerms.meaning: a man whose household squeezed pomegranates

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a pointless repeat of step 1. The גמרא quotes it again on purpose, to open a new discussion about רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: It raises a general question: whose behavior decides what counts as a 'normal' way of using an item for the laws of שבת?

phrases.english: Those of the house of Menashya bar Menachem
would squeeze pomegranates.
Rav Nachman said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּשֶׁל בֵּית מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר מְנַחֵם.
phrases.english: The halacha is like those of the house of Menashya bar Menachem.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: הֲלָכָה כְּשֶׁל בֵּית מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר מְנַחֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion based on the last clause of the ברייתא from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows the household of מנשיא בר מנחם. Pomegranates count as a squeezed fruit, so squeezing them on שבת is forbidden.

steps.title: רבא: מנשיא בן מנחם is not a תנא
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that one cannot say 'the הלכה follows' someone who is not a תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Is מנשיא בן מנחם a תנא?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges the way רב נחמן phrased his ruling. 'The הלכה follows X' is normally said about a sage, not a private household.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rulings like 'הלכה כ...' choose between the opinions of תנאים. מנשיא was just a man with a household custom, not a sage with an opinion. So the phrasing seems out of place.

keyTerms.meaning: a sage of the משנה era whose opinions are quoted

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Is Menashya ben Menachem a tanna?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: מְנַשְּׁיָא בֶּן מְנַחֵם תַּנָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's ruling from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's phrasing 'הלכה כשל בית מנשיא בר מנחם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'The הלכה follows' applies only to תנאים. מנשיא was not one.

steps.title: One household is not the majority of the world
steps.stepSummary: רבא blocks a possible defense. Even if רב נחמן meant the תנא who relied on this household, one family's habit is not what most people do.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the הלכה follows the תנא who held like the household of מנשיא בן מנחם, then is the הלכה like him just because he followed מנשיא בן מנחם? Is מנשיא בן מנחם the majority of the world?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers ahead of time a defense רב נחמן might give, and rejects it as well. The challenge to רב נחמן still stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe רב נחמן meant he rules like the תנא of the ברייתא, who relied on this household. But that תנא's whole reason is one family's custom. Whether a fruit counts as 'squeezed' should depend on what most people do, and one family is not most people.

keyTerms.meaning: the majority of the world (most people)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the principle that a 'normal' use of an item is measured by what most people do, not by the habits of a few individuals.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא הֲלָכָה כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא
phrases.english: And if you say: the halacha is like this tanna

phrases.aramaic: דְּסָבַר לַהּ כְּשֶׁל מְנַשְּׁיָא בֶּן מְנַחֵם,
phrases.english: who holds like [the practice of] those of Menashya ben Menachem,
then because he holds like Menashya ben Menachem,
is the halacha like him?

phrases.aramaic: מְנַשְּׁיָא בֶּן מְנַחֵם הָוֵי רוּבָּא דְּעָלְמָא?
phrases.english: Is Menashya ben Menachem the majority of the world?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הֲלָכָה כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's challenge by rejecting a possible re-reading of רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible reinterpretation of רב נחמן as ruling like the תנא of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That תנא relies only on one household's practice. What counts as a squeezed fruit should follow the majority of people, not one family.

steps.title: Proof from thorns kept in a vineyard
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers רבא: yes, a practice that not everyone follows can still count. He brings proof from רבי אליעזר, who says keeping thorns in a vineyard creates כלאים because people in ערביא grow thorns for camels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it can count, as we learned in a משנה: If someone keeps thorns growing in a vineyard, רבי אליעזר says he has made the vineyard forbidden as כלאים. The חכמים say only a plant that people normally keep makes it forbidden. רבי חנינא explained רבי אליעזר's reason: in ערביא people keep field thorns to feed their camels.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling. He shows that a practice found only in some places can still set the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had argued that one family's habit is not what most people do. רב נחמן answers that רבי אליעזר counts thorns as a crop everywhere just because they are grown in ערביא. So, he argues, a minority practice can still set the law.

keyTerms.meaning: One who keeps or maintains (a plant growing)
Made it forbidden (as כלאים in a vineyard)

phrases.english: Yes, as we learned (in a Mishnah):
One who keeps thorns growing in a vineyard,
Rabbi Eliezer says: he has made it forbidden,
phrases.notes: Forbidden as כלאים הכרם (mixed crops in a vineyard).

phrases.english: and the Sages say: nothing makes it forbidden
except a plant of a kind that people normally keep.
And Rabbi Chanina said:
What is Rabbi Eliezer's reason?
Because in Arabia they keep
field thorns to feed their camels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection in step 8 that one family's habit does not count.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a parallel source showing that a local or minority practice can set the הלכה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a practice followed by most people can set the law.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי אליעזר, a practice found in some places is enough.

steps.title: A whole country is different from one family
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the thorn proof. In ערביא a whole region grows thorns, but here only one family squeezes pomegranates, and one person's habit is outweighed by everyone else's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these really comparable? ערביא is an entire place. Here, one individual's way of thinking is cancelled out by the way all other people act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's proof and shows that the two cases are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A custom of a whole country carries weight. A single household's custom does not, because one person's view is cancelled out by what everyone else does. So the thorn case cannot support counting pomegranates as squeezable fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: His view is cancelled out by the practice of everyone else

phrases.english: Is this comparable?
Arabia is an entire place;
here, his view is cancelled out
by that of all other people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the thorns case and the pomegranate case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A whole region's custom counts, but one family's custom is outweighed by everyone else.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not reject רבי אליעזר's view about thorns. It only says that his reason (a whole country's custom) does not carry over to one family.

steps.title: A new reason: רב חסדא's ruling on beet juice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different reason for רב נחמן's ruling, based on רב חסדא. If someone squeezed beets and put the juice in a מקוה, the juice ruins the מקוה if it changes the water's color.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason, following רב חסדא. רב חסדא said: if someone squeezed beets and put the juice into a מקוה, the juice makes the מקוה invalid if it changes how the water looks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the thorn proof and sets up a new reason for רב נחמן's ruling. It starts by quoting רב חסדא's ruling about beet juice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea of 'one family's habit' is replaced with a new idea: the person's own intent. The beet juice case will show that once one person treats a juice as important, it counts as a liquid. The next step spells this out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is the reason (introduces a new explanation)
Change of appearance (color) of the water

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason: it follows Rav Chisda.
For Rav Chisda said:
Beets that one squeezed, and then put (the juice) in a mikveh
invalidate the mikveh if they change its appearance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10 rejected the thorn proof, this offers a new reason for רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the rejected reason with a different one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling depends on a widespread or regional practice.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling depends on the person who squeezes treating the juice as important (developed in the next step).

steps.title: Treating juice as important makes it a liquid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why רב חסדא's case proves the point. Beets are not normally squeezed, yet their juice counts as a liquid because the person treated it as important. The same applies to pomegranates.
steps.simpleTranslation: But beets are not normally squeezed, are they? So what must you say? Since he treated them as important, their juice counts as a liquid. Here too, since he treated the pomegranates as important, their juice counts as a liquid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from רב חסדא's case and applies it to the pomegranates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beets are not normally squeezed, so why would their juice count as a liquid? The only answer is that the person who squeezed them made the juice important. In the same way, the household of מנשיא בר מנחם made pomegranate juice important, so it counts as a liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: Things normally squeezed for their juice
A liquid (with the legal status of a drink)
Here too (applies the case to ours)

phrases.english: But beets are not things that are normally squeezed!
So what must you say?
Since he treated them as important,
their juice counts as a liquid.
Here too: since he treated them as important,
their juice counts as a liquid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from רב חסדא's ruling quoted in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's ruling that squeezed pomegranate juice counts as a liquid
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב חסדא's ruling that beet juice ruins a מקוה
steps.whyThisMatters: This introduces the idea that one person's intent (treating something as important) can give it legal status, even when most people do not treat it that way.

steps.title: רב פפא gives a different reason for the beet ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says beet juice ruins a מקוה for another reason. A מקוה cannot be made from it in the first place, and anything like that ruins a מקוה when it changes the water's color, even if it is not a 'liquid'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: beet juice ruins the מקוה because it is something you cannot make a מקוה from in the first place. Anything you cannot make a מקוה from in the first place ruins the מקוה when it changes how the water looks.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a different reason for רב חסדא's ruling. This takes away the proof the גמרא just built for רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 assumed beet juice ruins a מקוה only because it counts as a liquid. רב פפא says the real rule is that anything other than valid מקוה water ruins it by changing its color, whether or not it is a liquid. So the beet case says nothing about pomegranate juice counting as a liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, in the first place
One cannot make a ritual bath out of it

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is because it is something
from which one cannot make a mikveh in the first place,
and anything from which one cannot make
a mikveh in the first place
invalidates the mikveh if it changes its appearance.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין מִמֶּנּוּ מִקְוֶה לְכַתְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another reading of רב חסדא's ruling, which removes the proof from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רב חסדא's beet ruling as proof that intent makes juice a liquid
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The beet ruling depends on a separate מקוה rule (anything not valid for a מקוה ruins it by changing its color), not on the juice counting as a liquid.
steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא agrees that beet juice ruins the מקוה. He only disagrees about why, and that reason is what matters for the pomegranate question.
steps.whatToRemember: The thorn proof for רב נחמן was rejected, because a whole country differs from one family. The beet-juice support (via רב חסדא) depends on reading רב חסדא's ruling as being about a liquid. רב פפא explains that ruling with a separate מקוה rule, which would remove the support. The גמרא does not reject רב נחמן's ruling itself.

steps.title: A משנה about a מקוה: wine, vinegar, or olive discharge that changes its color
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from מקוואות. If wine, vinegar, or מוחל falls into a מקוה and changes the color of the water, the מקוה is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה there: if wine, vinegar, or olive discharge fell into a מקוה and changed how the water looks, the מקוה is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a new source, a משנה from מסכת מקוואות. It is setting up a question about who wrote this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists מוחל next to wine and vinegar, which are clearly liquids. That makes it look like the משנה treats מוחל as a real liquid too. This fits the earlier discussion of which juices count as a 'liquid' and which ones ruin a מקוה.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned there (in a משנה in another מסכת)
Olive discharge: the watery fluid from olives that is not oil
It changed its appearance (the water's color)

phrases.english: We learned there (in a mishnah in Mikvaot):

phrases.aramaic: נָפַל לְתוֹכוֹ יַיִן אוֹ חוֹמֶץ וּמוֹחַל,
phrases.english: If wine or vinegar or olive discharge fell into it (a mikveh),
and changed its appearance, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב פפא's point about beet juice ruining a מקוה, the גמרא brings a related משנה about liquids that change a מקוה's color.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine, vinegar, or מוחל that changes a מקוה's color makes the מקוה invalid.

steps.title: Who holds that olive discharge is a liquid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that מוחל counts as a liquid, since the משנה seems to assume it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that olive discharge is a liquid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the משנה follows. The משנה treats מוחל like a liquid, and not everyone agrees with that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the משנה invalidates the מקוה because מוחל is a liquid. If so, the משנה must follow a תנא who holds מוחל is a liquid.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (the author of this view)?

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who holds that olive discharge is a liquid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who wrote the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that מוחל has the status of a liquid.

steps.title: אביי: it is רבי יעקב, who holds olive discharge is a liquid
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה follows רבי יעקב. A ברייתא shows that רבי יעקב holds מוחל is a liquid. He explains that the first discharge is pure only because the owner does not want it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it is רבי יעקב. A ברייתא teaches that רבי יעקב says olive discharge is like a liquid. So why did the חכמים say that the discharge that comes out at the very beginning is pure? Because the owner does not want it to exist.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the משנה follows רבי יעקב. He backs this up with a ברייתא where רבי יעקב says מוחל is a liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that the first מוחל to come out is 'pure', meaning it does not make food able to become טמא. רבי יעקב explains that this is not because מוחל is not a liquid. It is because the owner does not want that early discharge, and a liquid only has this effect when its owner wants it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
What comes out at the very beginning
Pure; here it means it does not make food able to become טמא
He does not want it to exist (the owner is not happy with it)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'טהור' does not mean the מוחל itself is pure or impure. It means this discharge does not make food able to become טמא.

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is Rabbi Ya'akov.
As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Ya'akov says:
Olive discharge is like a liquid.
And why did they (the Sages) say
that olive discharge that comes out at the beginning is pure?
Because he (the owner) does not want it to exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of who wrote the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יעקב, who holds that מוחל is a liquid. The early discharge is pure only because the owner does not want it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: olive discharge is not a liquid
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא brings רבי שמעון's opposite view. מוחל is not a liquid. The discharge from the press bale makes food able to become טמא only because it always carries drops of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: olive discharge is not like a liquid. So why did they say that the discharge coming out of the bale of the olive press is impure? Because it cannot come out without little drops of oil in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון, who disagrees with רבי יעקב. He holds that מוחל is not a liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון also has a known rule to explain: the discharge from the press bale does make food able to become טמא. He says this is not because of the מוחל itself. It is because of the drops of real oil that always come out mixed in with it.

keyTerms.meaning: The bale (basket) of olives in the olive press
Impure; here it means it does make food able to become טמא

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Olive discharge is not like a liquid.
And why did they say

phrases.aramaic: מוֹחַל הַיּוֹצֵא מֵעִיקּוּל בֵּית הַבַּד טָמֵא —
phrases.english: that olive discharge coming out of the bale of the olive press is impure?

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ בְּלֹא צִיחְצוּחֵי שֶׁמֶן.
phrases.english: Because it is impossible for it to come out without drops of oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מוֹחַל אֵינוֹ כְּמַשְׁקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the view that disagrees with רבי יעקב. This shows that the משנה cannot follow רבי שמעון according to אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מוחל is not a liquid. The press-bale discharge counts only because of the oil drops mixed into it.

steps.title: What practical difference is there between them?
steps.stepSummary: Both opinions reach the same results in the two known cases, so the גמרא asks what practical difference their argument makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון agree on both known rules. It asks where their argument actually changes the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that the first discharge does not make food able to become טמא, and that the press-bale discharge does. They only explain these rules differently. So the גמרא looks for a case where the two explanations lead to different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the argument between רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where calling מוחל a liquid, or not, would change the הלכה.

steps.title: The difference: discharge that comes out after heavy pressing
steps.stepSummary: They argue about מוחל that comes out after the olives have been pressed hard. רבי יעקב says it is a liquid, and רבי שמעון says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difference between them: discharge that comes after heavy pressing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the case where the two opinions lead to different results: מוחל that comes out after heavy pressing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: That discharge is not the early, unwanted kind, so רבי יעקב's reason for calling the early discharge pure does not apply. It also comes after the heavy pressing has already squeezed the oil out, so it carries no oil drops, and רבי שמעון's reason for calling the press-bale discharge impure does not apply either. That leaves only their basic argument: רבי יעקב says it is a liquid, and רבי שמעון says it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them

phrases.english: There is a difference between them:
discharge that comes after heavy pressing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוחל that comes out after heavy pressing is a liquid for רבי יעקב, but not for רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבא: olive discharge ruins a מקוה for a different reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the משנה does not have to follow רבי יעקב. מוחל ruins a מקוה because a מקוה cannot be made from it, and anything like that ruins a מקוה when it changes the water's color.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: it is because olive discharge is something a מקוה cannot be made from, and such a thing ruins a מקוה when it changes the water's appearance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the question 'who wrote the משנה?' He says the משנה does not need to treat מוחל as a liquid at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי tied the משנה to רבי יעקב because he assumed only a liquid can ruin a מקוה. רבא says the real reason is different: you cannot make a מקוה out of מוחל, and anything you cannot make a מקוה from ruins one when it changes the color. So even רבי שמעון could agree with the משנה. This is the same reasoning רב פפא used about beet juice in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Something a מקוה cannot be made from

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that ruining a מקוה through a color change does not depend on whether something is a 'liquid'. It depends on whether a מקוה could be made from it. This takes away the proof that the משנה must follow רבי יעקב.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין הֵימֶנּוּ מִקְוֶה,
phrases.english: It is because it is something from which a mikveh cannot be made,
and such a thing invalidates the mikveh by changing its appearance.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין הֵימֶנּוּ מִקְוֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the question of who wrote the משנה and gives a different answer from אביי's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה does not depend on מוחל being a liquid. It ruins a מקוה because a מקוה cannot be made from it.

steps.title: שמואל: on שבת you may squeeze grapes into a pot, but not into a bowl
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: on שבת a person may squeeze a cluster of grapes into a pot of food, but not into an empty bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a person may squeeze a cluster of grapes into a pot, but not into a bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about squeezing on שבת. The topic moves back from מקוה to the laws of שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Squeezing juice out of fruit is normally forbidden on שבת. Squeezing into a pot of food is different, because the juice goes straight into food. Squeezing into an empty bowl is not allowed, because the juice is collected on its own as a drink.

keyTerms.meaning: A cooking pot (with food in it)

steps.confusionAlert: The pot here has food in it, so the juice becomes part of that food. The bowl here is empty, so the juice is just a drink.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: סוֹחֵט אָדָם אֶשְׁכּוֹל שֶׁל עֲנָבִים לְתוֹךְ הַקְּדֵרָה,
phrases.english: A person may squeeze a cluster of grapes into a pot (of food),
but not into an (empty) bowl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about squeezing on שבת, after the discussion of what counts as a liquid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת you may squeeze grapes into a pot of food, but not into an empty bowl.

steps.title: רב חסדא: so you may also milk a goat into a pot
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns from שמואל's ruling that on שבת you may milk a goat into a pot of food, but not into an empty bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: from what our teacher said, we can learn that a person may milk a goat into a pot, but not into a bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא takes שמואל's grape ruling and applies it to a new case: milking a goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Milking is like squeezing, because it takes a liquid out of where it is held. If grape juice that goes into food is allowed, then milk that goes straight into food should be allowed too. Milking into an empty bowl is still not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: From the words of our teacher (שמואל) we learn

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
From the words of our teacher we learn:
A person may milk a goat into a pot (of food),
but not into an (empty) bowl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies שמואל's grape ruling to milking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת you may milk a goat into a pot of food, but not into an empty bowl.

steps.title: The principle: a liquid that goes into food counts as food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the idea behind these rulings: a liquid that goes straight into food is treated as food, not as a drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems he holds that a liquid that goes into food is food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls out the general rule behind רב חסדא's (and שמואל's) rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Squeezing is forbidden on שבת because it produces a liquid. If the liquid goes straight into food, it counts as food from the start. So squeezing or milking into a pot of food does not count as producing a liquid. This explains why the pot is allowed and the empty bowl is not.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid that goes into food is food

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ideas here. First, מוחל ruins a מקוה either because it is a liquid (אביי's reading, following רבי יעקב) or because a מקוה cannot be made from it (רבא). Second, on שבת a liquid squeezed or milked straight into food counts as food, so it is allowed into a pot of food but not into an empty bowl.

phrases.english: So it seems he holds
that a liquid that comes into food is food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the principle behind רב חסדא's milking ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A liquid that goes straight into food is treated as food, so squeezing or milking into a pot of food is allowed on שבת.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא's challenge from a זב who milks a goat
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא challenges the rule from a משנה that says milk milked by a זב is טמא. If the milk counts as food, nothing made it able to become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא objected: a משנה teaches that if a זב milks a goat, the milk is impure. But if you say that a liquid going straight into food counts as food, then with what was this milk made able to become impure?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks the rule from the last step using a משנה about a זב who milks a goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can only become טמא after a liquid has touched it first. This is called הכשר. If milk going into food counts as food, then the milk itself is not a liquid, so no liquid ever touched it. So how could the משנה call it טמא?

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
A man who is impure because of a certain bodily discharge. He makes things impure even by moving them.
Was made susceptible, meaning able to become impure, by contact with a liquid

steps.confusionAlert: Food does not become impure just by touching something impure. First it must get wet from one of the special liquids (הכשר). That missing first step is the whole problem here.

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama raised an objection:
a zav who milks the goat
the milk is impure.
And if you say
a liquid that comes into food is food,
phrases.notes: This quotes the rule from step 23.

phrases.english: with what was it made susceptible to impurity?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle stated in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a liquid going straight into food counts as food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the milk is food, no liquid ever wet it. Without a liquid there is no הכשר, so the milk could not be טמא. Yet the משנה says it is טמא.

steps.title: The drop on the tip of the teat makes the milk susceptible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers using רבי יוחנן's idea. The first drop smeared on the tip of the teat is a real liquid, and it makes the milk able to become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in another place, it is made susceptible through the drop that is smeared on the tip of the teat. Here too, it is made susceptible through the drop smeared on the tip of the teat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רמי בר חמא's question. It points to a small first drop of milk that does count as a liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first drop smears on the tip of the teat and is not meant to go into the food. So it keeps its status as a liquid. That drop touches the rest of the milk and gives it הכשר. The rule from step 23 stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: The smeared drop, the first bit of milk that wets the area
The opening, or tip, of the teat
Here too. It applies an idea from another case to this one.

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule "a liquid going into food is food" survives. It only covers milk that actually goes into the food, not the stray drop on the teat.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said:
through the drop smeared on the tip of the teat,
here too:
through the drop smeared on the tip of the teat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a separate liquid source that provides the הכשר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No liquid touched the milk, so it could not become impure
steps.terutzMaskana: The first drop on the teat is a true liquid and makes the milk susceptible

steps.title: רבינא begins a challenge from a corpse-impure person squeezing olives and grapes
steps.stepSummary: רבינא starts a new objection from a משנה about a טמא מת who squeezes olives and grapes. The challenge is completed on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא objected: a person who is impure from a dead body and squeezed olives and grapes...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up a new challenge. רבינא begins quoting a משנה about a טמא מת who squeezes olives and grapes. The rest of the quote and the question come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Squeezing olives and grapes produces liquids, oil and wine. רבינא will use this case to test the rule that a liquid going into food counts as food. The actual point of attack comes in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is impure from contact with a dead body

phrases.english: Ravina raised an objection:
one impure from a corpse who squeezed olives and grapes,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second challenge to the principle from step 23, after the first one was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a liquid going straight into food counts as food
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet fully stated. The משנה about squeezing olives and grapes will be used against the rule on the next amud.
